text:
alice: Quick sync — dropping a short proposal to rationalize the service catalog with a dependency "thermal map" + ownership runway. doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/service-catalog-thermal-map :eyes:
ben: skimmed it. love the idea of a heatmap to focus paydown. curious how you score "heat" vs "value" though?
clara: +1 on focusing. we also need a safe migration pattern for modules that have wide fanout (billing, auth). can we cohort by consumer surface?
diego: Agree with cohorting. Proposed triage scoring (very rough):
```
heat_score = (error_rate * 0.4) + (deploy_churn * 0.3) + (p99_latency_rank * 0.2) + (owner_unavailability * 0.1)
value_score = downstream_consumers * revenue_impact
priority = heat_score * 0.7 + normalize(value_score) * 0.3
```
alice: That matches my intent. The doc has a spreadsheet with numbers for all ~120 services. I can export a small sample to show the top 12 hotspots.
ben: Can you paste the sample here? short list is fine.
alice: Pasted sample top-5:
- service-slate: heat 8.7, value 3.2 (many tenants)
- session-captain: heat 7.9, value 6.0 (paths blocked on retries)
- model-proxy: heat 7.5, value 9.1 (latency sensitive)
- quota-enricher: heat 7.2, value 2.0
- telemetry-ingest: heat 6.8, value 4.5

clara: model-proxy being high-value + hot makes it a candidate for an early refactor into a slim facade + dedicated runtime. but that feels risky. thoughts on a 2-step plan?
diego: 2-step = (1) facade adapter that isolates protocol + contracts, (2) gradual internal refactor behind facade with canary routing. keep read-only stable.
ben: we should also add an automated compatibility test harness to gate merges. If facade preserves the contract we can do straight A/B by header route.
alice: Exactly. I've sketched the canary plan in the doc: small percents in low-traffic regions -> monitor errors, tail latency, and tokenized cost.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: #deploy-checks 1719907801. Runbook template attached.
clara: Nice. On the ownership runway: propose 3 buckets for each service — maintain, rationalize, deprecate. Each bucket gets a 3/6/12 month runway and a responsible pair (owner + steward).
diego: Deprecation runway needs consumer migration quotas and a compatibility shim for 6 months if needed. Also add a migration deadline to the service manifest.
ben: how do we fund this work? reclaim weekly 25% of eng-sprint from platform backlog each quarter? or create a dedicated debt sprint every 6 weeks?
alice: My recommendation is hybrid: small steady allocation (15% per sprint) plus a focused 6-week debt sprint per quarter for the top 10 items. That keeps progress visible.
clara: Need metrics to show impact: reduction in cross-service incidents, deploy flakiness, and end-to-end p99 improvement. propose a dashboard with three lines.
alice: I'll wire up a dashboard in Console and tag the initial tickets. planning to present the heatmap + prioritized backlog at next architect sync.
diego: One last ask — add a safety metric: consumer-backwards-compat failures; if >0.1% we rollback.
ben: +1. Also add a canary playbook for model-proxy showing how to toggle routing via feature flag and fallback to legacy.
alice: will do. thanks all. schedule: draft RFC by Friday, kickoff next Tue. :calendar:
ben: thanks, this feels actionable. :thumbsup:
clara: Thanks — excited to see the RFC.
